title: Work IQ: business skills for agents through Work IQ MCP
summary: Microsoft has deferred automatic enablement for existing environments from November 2026, so the briefing's rollout warning is no longer accurate. Current documentation also does not substantiate the September 30 start date or the promise to enable EU and EFTA environments at general availability. The documented control paths and Allowed MCP Clients API are supported.

claims.claim: Business skills are natural-language instructions capturing organisational business processes.
claims.quote: Business skills are natural-language instructions that capture how your organization gets work done. They represent your business processes, policies, and domain knowledge in a format that agents can understand and follow.

claims.claim: A skill describes process steps, required information and business rules.
claims.quote: Each skill describes how to complete a specific type of work—the steps involved, the information required, and the business rules that apply.

claims.claim: Agents discover and use accessible skills at runtime through Work IQ MCP.
claims.quote: Agents discover and use the business skills they have access to as needed at runtime using Work IQ MCP to complete tasks according to your organization's processes.

claims.claim: Multiple agents using the same skill follow the same process.
claims.quote: When multiple agents use the same skill, they follow the same process, ensuring consistent behavior across your organization.

claims.claim: Business skills are stored in Dataverse.
claims.quote: Business skills are stored in Dataverse and follow Dataverse security patterns.

claims.claim: Skills have frontmatter containing a name, description and metadata.
claims.quote: Frontmatter | Name, description, and optional key-value metadata

claims.claim: Skills contain full process instructions.
claims.quote: Instructions | Full skill body | Contains the complete process definition

claims.claim: Agents query frontmatter to identify relevant skills.

claims.quote: Business skills are not executable code. They contain natural-language instructions that guide agent behavior

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Work IQ has an on-by-default route for eligible environments, represented by defaultState on.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants.
claims.fix: Keep defaultState on, but qualify the default as applying to eligible new public production environments. Note that https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/settings-features#dataverse-intelligence-preview separately lists 'Turn on Dataverse intelligence (Work IQ) for agents and AI experiences' with default Off.

claims.claim: Microsoft starts default enablement for eligible new environments on September 30, 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "September 30, 2026"; read default-settings, manage-participation and quickstart. Current default-settings confirms eligible new environments are on by default but supplies no September 30 start date.
claims.fix: Replace the dated new-environment clause with: 'Microsoft Learn says Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants, subject to the exceptions below.'

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters: existing-environment warning
claims.claim: Microsoft starts default enablement for eligible existing environments in November 2026.
claims.quote: The plan to turn on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptionshas been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule. Check this article for updates.
claims.fix: Replace the existing-environment November statement with: 'Microsoft has deferred the previously documented November 2026 plan to turn on Business Applications in Work IQ for eligible existing environments; the current page gives no replacement date.' Replace the Why it matters warning with: 'Review whether existing environments should participate; Microsoft has deferred their automatic enablement from November 2026.'

claims.claim: The documented automatic default applies to public production environments.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants.

claims.claim: EU and EFTA environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned in the EU and EFTA macro region geography.

claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: Government-related environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Trial, sandbox and developer environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: Nonproduction environments: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.where: What's changing: EU/EFTA parenthesis; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft plans to enable EU and EFTA environments by default when the feature becomes generally available.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "EFTA" "generally available"; read default-settings and returned Work IQ excerpts. Current default-settings lists EU/EFTA as exceptions but gives no general-availability trigger for their default enablement.
claims.fix: Remove 'Microsoft plans to enable them when the feature becomes generally available' from What's changing. In Open questions, retain only: 'On what date will EU and EFTA environments be enabled by default?'

claims.claim: Customers outside the automatic default can opt in using the corresponding Microsoft 365 admin center setting, alongside environment enablement.
claims.quote: If Business Applications in Work IQ isn't on by default in your environment, you can turn it on. Turn on the tenant-level setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center and the environment-level setting in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: A Power Platform administrator can manually turn on Work IQ in the environment.
claims.quote: To enable business skills in a Dataverse environment, a Power Platform administrator turns on Work IQ.

Enable business skills in Dataverse for Sales agent (preview)

claims.claim: Business skills require Work IQ to be enabled in the Dataverse environment.
claims.quote: A Dataverse environment with Work IQ enabled by a Power Platform administrator.

claims.claim: Agent skill selection is probabilistic.
claims.quote: Agent selection is probabilistic, so test representative requests before you share a skill broadly.

claims.claim: Skill ownership controls access.

claims.claim: Sharing governs who can read or edit a skill and its associated content.
claims.quote: Direct access—Shares the skill with specific users or groups and lets you choose whether they can view or edit the skill.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls

claims.quote: Governance—Control who can create, modify, and use business skills through ownership, sharing, and Dataverse security roles.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Security-role sharing requires both the selected Dataverse role and Skill Sharing Role.
claims.quote: Users who access a skill through a Dataverse security role must have both the selected role and the Skill Sharing Role security role.

claims.claim: General access and direct access are distinct skill-sharing methods.
claims.quote:
General access—Makes the skill available to everyone in the environment.
Direct access—Shares the skill with specific users or groups

claims.claim: Environment Work IQ participation is controlled in Power Platform admin center at Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Power Platform admin center.
Select Manage, and select the environment.
Select Settings > Product > Features.
Locate Work IQ.
Turn on Work IQ if it's currently off.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for the environment Work IQ participation switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ environment PowerShell API enable settings; Work IQ enable environment pac admin Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironment; Work IQ environment Power Platform API enable. Read manage-participation, default-settings and quickstart; no setting-specific call found.

claims.claim: The tenant control is in Microsoft 365 admin center at Copilot > Settings > View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation pane, select Copilot > Settings.
In Copilot settings, select View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API for the tenant Business Applications data availability setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Applications data Copilot Graph settings API; Copilot Dataverse tenant Graph settings API enable. Read default-settings, manage-ai-experience-access and returned Graph permissions excerpts; no endpoint for this control found.

claims.claim: Environment Allowed MCP Clients is reached in Power Platform admin center through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Advanced Settings > Allowed MCP Clients.
claims.quote:
Go to Manage > Environments, and then select the environment.
On the command bar, select Settings.
Expand Product, and then select Features.
In the Dataverse Model Context Protocol section, select Go to Advanced Settings.
In Advanced Settings > Allowed MCP Clients
